ckpt_name.tooltip: The name of the checkpoint (model) to load.

sampler_name.tooltip: The algorithm used when sampling, this can affect the quality, speed, and style of the generated output.

scheduler.tooltip: The scheduler controls how noise is gradually removed to form the image.

audio_vae.tooltip: The Audio VAE model to use for encoding.

video_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the video mask.

video_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the video mask.

audio_start_time.tooltip: Start time in seconds for the audio mask.

audio_end_time.tooltip: End time in seconds for the audio mask.

max_length.tooltip: 'truncate': cut latent to end_time length. 'pad': extend latent to end_time. 'partial': mask range within existing latent.

existing_mask_mode.tooltip: How to combine with existing noise masks if present. 'add' will take the max of existing and new mask, 'overwrite' will replace with new mask. 'subtract' will set the masked region to 0 instead of 1, effectively unmasking it.

model_version.tooltip: Tiny: Fast, good quality. Tiny Long: Slower, uses much less VRAM for long videos. Full: Best quality, highest VRAM.

scale.tooltip: The upscaling factor. 4x is recommended for best quality.

enable_tiling.tooltip: Process the video in tiles. Slower, but saves a large amount of VRAM.

tile_size.tooltip: The height/width of each tile (before upscaling). Larger tiles are faster but use more VRAM. Recommended: 384-512 for HD videos.

tile_overlap.tooltip: The amount of overlap between tiles to prevent visible seams. Recommended: 48-64 for smooth blending. (Must be < Tile Size / 2)

speed_optimization.tooltip: Higher value (e.g., 2.0) is faster but may capture less fine detail. Lower (e.g., 1.5) is slower but more detailed.

quality_boost.tooltip: Increases quality and detail preservation at the cost of more VRAM. (Higher = Better Quality)

stability_level.tooltip: Controls temporal stability. 11 is more stable (default). 9 can be sharper but may have less temporal consistency.

color_fix.tooltip: Applies a color correction step to prevent potential color shifts from the original video.

vae_tiling.tooltip: Enables tiling for the VAE decoding step. Further reduces VRAM usage, especially for high-resolution output.

unload_model.tooltip: Unload the main model from VRAM before decoding frames with the VAE. Saves VRAM but is slightly slower.

sageattention.tooltip: Enable SageAttention optimization for faster inference (~20-30% speedup). Disable if encountering compatibility issues.

device.tooltip: Select the processing device. 'auto' will try to pick the best one available (CUDA > MPS > CPU).

precision.tooltip: Processing precision. BF16 is often faster on modern GPUs. FP16 is a good alternative.

seed.tooltip: The random seed for the diffusion process.

original_resized_images.tooltip: The original resized image before pre-processing, used as reference.

color_correction_method.tooltip: Method to match the generated image colors to the original image. lab: transfer color in CIELAB space, preserving detail (most faithful). wavelet: transfer low-frequency color, keeping upscaled high-frequency detail. adain: match per-channel mean/std (fastest, global tint). none: skip color transfer (geometry alignment only).

latent.tooltip: The VAE-encoded SeedVR2 latent to split.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: Latent frames shared between adjacent chunks and crossfaded at merge; 0 = no overlap.

chunking_mode.tooltip: manual = use frames_per_chunk exactly; auto = predict the largest chunk that fits free VRAM.

latents.tooltip: The sampled temporal chunks in sequence order.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: The temporal_overlap output of Split SeedVR2 Latent. 0 = plain concatenation.

temporal_size.tooltip: Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to encode at a time.

temporal_overlap.tooltip: Only used for video VAEs: Amount of frames to overlap.

bg_removal_name.tooltip: The model used to remove backgrounds from images

bg_removal_model.tooltip: Background removal model used to generate the mask

image.tooltip: Input image to remove the background from

refine_iterations.tooltip: SAM decoder refinement passes (0=use raw detector masks)

individual_masks.tooltip: Output per-object masks instead of union

positive_coords.tooltip: Positive point prompts as JSON [{"x": int, "y": int}, ...] (pixel coords)

negative_coords.tooltip: Negative point prompts as JSON [{"x": int, "y": int}, ...] (pixel coords)

strength_start.tooltip: Control strength at the start of sampling (high sigma).

strength_end.tooltip: Control strength at the end of sampling (low sigma). Linearly interpolated from start.

restore_cfg.tooltip: Pulls denoised output toward the input latent. Higher = stronger fidelity to input. 0 to disable.

restore_cfg_s_tmin.tooltip: Sigma threshold below which restore_cfg is disabled.
